approaches.hypothesis: these steps solve this class of problem
approaches.name: A1

pipeline.title: Reproduce: build a scenario tree with a normal file and a nested subdir matched by an ignore-paths regex, run PyLinter._discover_files + expand_modules on it with various invocation forms (bare relative dir, '.', trailing slash) to confirm which forms bypass the filter

Locate every place a discovered/candidate path is compared against ignore_list_paths_re: pylint/lint/pylinter.py _discover_files (root check) and pylint/lint/expand_modules.py _is_ignored_file/_is_in_ignore_list_re (top-level arg check and subfilepath check)

Determine why the regex fails to match: the string being tested still carries filesystem artifacts (leading './', OS-specific separators) that the anchored user-supplied pattern does not expect, because normalization (os.path.normpath) happens only after the ignore check, or not at all on some code paths

Fix by normalizing the path (os.path.normpath, and converting to a consistent separator via the existing regexp_paths_csv dual-pattern compile) before every ignore_list_paths_re comparison, in both _discover_files and expand_modules, so the same file is judged the same way regardless of how it was reached (top-level arg, os.walk root, or package sub-walk)

Verify: re-run the reproduction scenarios (bare dir, '.', trailing slash, package-with-__init__ case) and confirm the ignored subdir's files are absent from expand_modules' result in all of them; also run pylint's existing ignore-paths/recursive test suite

approaches.source: issue.md (bug report) + direct reproduction via pylint.lint.pylinter.PyLinter._discover_files and pylint.lint.expand_modules.expand_modules called on a scenario tree, confirming ignore-paths match failure is caused by un-normalized paths (e.g. leading './') reaching the ignore-list regex check before os.path.normpath is applied

fom.measure: Build a temp directory tree with a top-level dir (no __init__.py) containing a normal .py file and a nested subdir (e.g. gen/) also without __init__.py containing .py files that should be excluded. Run pylint programmatically with --recursive=y and ignore-paths set to a pattern matching the nested subdir (e.g. '^dir/gen/.*$'), using pylint.lint.expand_modules.expand_modules and pylinter._discover_files directly (or via Run()). Count: (number of scenarios where files under the ignored subdir are absent from the discovered/expanded file list) / (total scenarios tried). Include a scenario with forward-slash pattern vs backslash path (simulating Windows via os.path with sep) if feasible, plus a plain relative-path scenario, since the bug is path-separator/anchoring dependent.
fom.name: recursive_ignore_paths_pass_rate

set -e
WORK=$(mktemp -d)
mkdir -p "$WORK/src/gen"
printf 'x = 1\n' > "$WORK/src/gen/about.py"
printf 'y = 2\n' > "$WORK/src/main.py"
if [ "top-level-file" = "nested-package-init" ]; then
  touch "$WORK/src/gen/__init__.py"

if [ "pylintrc" = "pylintrc" ]; then
  printf '[MASTER]\nignore=about.py\n' > "$WORK/.pylintrc"
else
  printf '[tool.pylint.MASTER]\nignore = ["about.py"]\n' > "$WORK/pyproject.toml"
fi
if [ "relative" = "absolute" ]; then
  TARGET="$WORK/src"
else
  TARGET="src"
fi
cd "$WORK"
if [ "recursive" = "recursive" ]; then
  python -m pylint --recursive=y "$TARGET" > out.txt 2>&1 || true
else
  python -m pylint "$TARGET" "$TARGET/gen" > out.txt 2>&1 || true
fi
grep -q "main.py" out.txt && ! grep -q "about.py" out.txt
